definition: The Inception Score (IS) is an algorithm used to assess the quality of images created by a generative image model such as a generative adversarial network (GAN).
details: The score is calculated based on the output of a separate, pretrained Inception v3 image classification model applied to a sample of (typically around 30,000) images generated by the generative model. The Inception Score is maximized when the following conditions are true: The entropy of the distribution of labels predicted by the Inceptionv3 model for the generated images is minimized. In other words, the classification model confidently predicts a single label for each image. Intuitively, this corresponds to the desideratum of generated images being "sharp" or "distinct". The predictions of the classification model are evenly distributed across all possible labels. This corresponds to the desideratum that the output of the generative model is "diverse". It has been somewhat superseded by the related Fréchet inception distance. While the Inception Score only evaluates the distribution of generated images, the FID compares the distribution of generated images with the distribution of a set of real images ("ground truth").

explainer.lead: The Inception Score gives a single number for judging images made by a generative model. It rewards images that a separate classifier can label confidently and a collection whose labels are varied, offering a combined signal for distinctness and diversity.

tiers.eli5: Imagine asking an art student to draw many kinds of things, then showing the drawings to a judge. Clear drawings that the judge can easily name score well, and so does a collection with many different subjects rather than the same thing repeatedly. The Inception Score turns those two ideas into one number.
tiers.practitioner: Run a pretrained Inception v3 classifier on a sample of generated images, typically around 30,000, and calculate the score from its label predictions. A high score requires confident per-image predictions and an even spread across labels, so a model can score poorly through unclear images or limited variety. It does not compare outputs with real images; Fréchet inception distance adds that comparison and has somewhat superseded IS.
tiers.paperLevel: For generated images x, let p(y|x) be the Inception v3 label distribution and p(y) its average over the sample; IS = exp(E_x[KL(p(y|x) || p(y))]). The score is favored by low entropy in each p(y|x) and high entropy in p(y), corresponding to confident labels and diverse predictions. Its main limitation is that it evaluates only the generated distribution, without comparison to a ground-truth distribution of real images.

explainer.example: Suppose a model generates 30,000 images and Inception v3 confidently assigns a single label to each one. If those labels are evenly spread across all possible labels, the model receives a high score; if the images are hard to classify or the sample uses only a few labels, the score is lower.

usedIn.name: Generative image model evaluation
usedIn.detail: Used to summarize classifier predictions on a large sample of generated images as one quality score.

explainer.goal: Assess a generative image model by rewarding both clearly classifiable individual images and diversity across the generated sample.
inputs: A sample of generated images, typically around 30,000
A separate pretrained Inception v3 image classifier
outputs: A higher score when labels are confident and evenly distributed
steps: Generate a sample of images with the model being evaluated.
Pass every sampled image through the pretrained Inception v3 classifier.
Check that each image receives a confident prediction for one label.
Check that predictions across the sample are evenly spread over the possible labels.
Combine these properties into the final Inception Score.
tradeoffs: Captures both image distinctness and sample diversity
Does not compare generated images with real images
Confident classification alone is not enough without diverse labels
Fréchet inception distance has somewhat superseded it
